items.title: AI worsens climate change, integrated assessment shows
items.desc: Embeds AI's effects on emissions, output and climate damages into the DICE integrated-assessment model, separating an 'ICT-like' AI scenario from an 'Industrial-Revolution-like' one. Finds AI is net polluting, adding roughly 0.1-0.8 C by 2100, with climate costs offsetting about a fifth to a quarter of AI's economic gains. [arXiv econ.GN, announced 2026-08-26 (submitted 2026-08-24/25)]

items.title: Learning Whom to Trust: Decision-Generated Credibility in Social Learning
items.desc: Reinforcement-learning agents make binary choices through a drift-diffusion process, and their own decision confidence becomes the credibility weight that other agents place on their advice. Moderate social transmission speeds up collective correction, while strong transmission can lock a population into a wrong consensus. [arXiv econ.GN / cs.NE, announced 2026-08-26 (submitted 2026-08-24/25)]

items.title: Political Entrepreneurs
items.desc: Links state legislators' financial disclosures to bill sponsorship across 26 states from 2009 to 2023, using a large language model to classify bill text as pro-business and pro-entry. Entrepreneur-legislators, about 40% of the sample, turn out not to be generic business advocates but to selectively push deregulation and entry-lowering bills. [NBER, posted 2026-08-24]

items.title: Harvesting the Volatility Risk Premium: A Learning-to-Rank Approach
items.desc: Uses a LightGBM LambdaRank learning-to-rank model to choose daily among nine short-put strategies on zero-day-to-expiry S&P 500 weekly options, adding margin-aware position sizing and a model-uncertainty abstention rule. Reports out-of-time Sharpe ratios of 4.3 to 5.8 against passive put-writing benchmarks. [arXiv q-fin, announced 2026-08-26 (submitted 2026-08-24/25)]

items.title: Lead-Lag Relationships in Financial Markets: A Comparison of Multiple Clustering Algorithms
items.desc: Benchmarks three machine-learning time-series clustering methods (MiniRocket-KMeans, KShape, and a KShape/DTW-KMedoids ensemble) against standard DTW-KMedoids for constructing lead-lag trading strategies. MiniRocket-KMeans performs best under the lead strategy, and tuning the cluster count by silhouette score improves robustness. [arXiv q-fin, announced 2026-08-26 (submitted 2026-08-24/25)]

items.title: findr: Transparent and Fair Credit Risk Decisions through Semi-Structured Regressions
items.desc: Splits a credit-scoring model's logit into an interpretable linear component plus an orthogonal neural-network residual, with a Wasserstein penalty during training to limit disparities across demographic groups. It behaves like logistic regression when the signal is linear but recovers most of a neural network's accuracy when it is not. [arXiv q-fin.RM / cs.LG, announced 2026-08-26 (submitted 2026-08-24/25)]

items.title: Bill Gates says he's worried AI will harm workers, kids and society
items.desc: Gates, long an AI optimist, now says he would rather the technology advanced more slowly, citing worker displacement among his concerns. The piece is framed as a wide-ranging interview on societal harms rather than a tight economic analysis. [Washington Post, 2026-08-26]

items.title: Wall Street Journal says AI-generated op-ed didn't breach its standards
items.desc: The WSJ defended running an op-ed that investor Stanley Druckenmiller wrote with AI assistance criticising Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's market interventions. The story sits in the Business section but is chiefly about newsroom AI-disclosure policy. [Washington Post, 2026-08-25]
